source.title: The Bonds You Don't See
source.summary: Your mortgage, your pension, your savings account: they all run through the bond market. How ordinary people became unwitting participants in the world's largest riba system.
source.author: Islamic Economics
source.body_text: When you take out a mortgage, your loan gets packaged, securitized, and sold as bonds to investors around the world. Your monthly payment funds someone's retirement in Norway. Your student loan is a bond. Your savings account earns interest because your bank lends your money out and buys bonds. The 2008 financial crisis wasn't really a housing crisis. It was a bond market crisis: mortgage-backed securities that nobody understood collapsed, and the entire global economy nearly went with them. This episode traces how bonds touch every aspect of ordinary life, and how the hadith about riba's dust reaching everyone has become literally true in the modern financial system.
